0.1.unit: D-400 flashes a cold n-butane / n-hexane feed (16 m³/h, ≈ 10208 kg/h, 35 wt% C4 at design) after the hot-oil preheater E-400 (TIC-401 holds 74 °C through the 3-way TCV-401) and the let-down valve FCV-400 (FIC-400). The drum runs at 102.7 kPa g (PIC-420 → PCV-420 to the fuel-gas header) with 50 % level (LIC-400 → LCV-400 to the receiver). Design products: vapour 611 Nm³/h at 76.8 wt% C4 (spec ≥ 75), liquid 14.0 m³/h at 26.6 wt% C4 (spec ≤ 28); flash 49.2 °C; margin 424 $/h.

0.4.ctx: Unit lined out at design this morning. After lunch the bottoms analyser creeps toward its spec and the vapour flow is higher; the controllers have not been touched. Day shift, normal weather; no maintenance on the unit.

R.1.p: D-400 is a single equilibrium stage: the hot feed is let down into the drum and splits into a vapour and a liquid at the drum temperature and pressure. At a fixed T and P the compositions of the two phases are fixed by the phase equilibrium (T–x–y); the feed composition only changes how much of each phase forms (lever rule). So a lighter feed at the same T and P gives more vapour, and the liquid follows the bubble-point line: at the same pressure a liquid with more butane boils at a lower temperature. To strip more butane out of the liquid, the flash needs more heat (higher TIC-401) or a lower pressure (PIC-420).

R.2.eq: F·z = V·y + L·x      V/F = (z − x)/(y − x)      Q_E-400 = ṁ·cp·(T_out − T_in) + flash

1.4.why: Only product quality is at stake and it moves slowly; no trip, relief or equipment limit is close. 1.5.sp: A reduced, stable state that stops a problem growing while you investigate (not needed here: nothing is near a limit).
1.5.tc: A consequence for people, environment or equipment arrives before the diagnosis is done unless you act now (here only the product spec, slowly).

1.6.p: At fixed T and P a flash fixes the phase compositions; the feed composition sets how much vapour forms — and the bubble point of the liquid tells the composition.

3.2.n: Butane balance: the two outlets carry 3780 kg/h of C4 in 10141 kg/h, i.e. 37.3 wt% of what comes in; with the design 35 wt% feed only 3549 kg/h of C4 would enter, so the balance does not close unless the feed is lighter. The flash temperature tells the same story: at the same pressure the liquid now boils 1.2 °C lower, i.e. it holds more butane. The heat side is at design (TCV-401 30.4 %, TI-403 120 °C), so the feed got lighter, not the heat lower.

5.7.n: AI-410 kept rising for a few minutes (it reached 28.16 wt%: the liquid in the drum turns over slowly) and was below 28 wt% from 00:29:40, 5 min after the move. The AI-410 HI alarm cleared only at 00:46:33: AI-410 had to fall below 27.72 wt% (1 % deadband). At 01:04:40: AI-410 27.63, AI-420 78.01 wt%, FI-420 753 Nm³/h, TI-410 47.47 °C, TCV-401 35.3 %, E-400 446 kW (design 420), margin 429 $/h (design 424). Actual matched the offline prediction to within 0.01 wt%. 77.5 °C would have left AI-410 at 27.75, inside the alarm deadband.

5.8.rule: When both products move and the controllers have not, look at the feed before the instruments: ask what changed upstream and sample it.

6.0.n: The offline copy predicted the final AI-410 and AI-420; the recovery took longer than the move because the drum liquid had to turn over.

6.3.fut: A unit without a feed analyser sees a feed change only through its products: any switch of supply needs a sample and a call.

6.4.how: Without the diagnosis the bottoms would have settled at ≈ 28.81 wt% (off spec) with a margin of ≈ -158 $/h; after the fix ≈ 429 $/h. 587 $/h × 8 h (one shift until the tank is changed, assumed).

6.5.again:
Read the trends from the start before moving anything.
Compare the products with the settings: products moved, settings did not → look upstream.
Predict the move on a copy, then make it once.
6.5.never:
Never blame the analyser without a lab sample.
Never chase an off-spec product with heat alone up to the alarm limit.

hyp.cause: The feed is lighter than design (new tank): more butane enters than the flash at 74 °C / 102.7 kPa g can take overhead
hyp.ifthen: If the feed is lighter, the same T and P flash more vapour (FI-420 ↑) and leave more butane in the liquid (AI-410 ↑, FI-410 ↓); the bubble point falls, so TI-410 falls; heat input and pressure stay at design; a lab feed sample shows > 35 wt% C4
hyp.key: FI-420 ↑ with AI-410 ↑ and TI-410 ↓ at constant TIC/PIC; outlet C4 balance > 35 wt%; lab feed > 35 wt%
hyp.fals: Lab feed at 35 wt%, or FI-420 falling, or the heat input off design

hyp.cause: Less heat into the feed than the board shows (TT-401 reading high, E-400 fouled, hot oil cooler)
hyp.ifthen: If the feed were really colder, less would flash: FI-420 falls, AI-420 rises a little, TCV-401 or TI-403 moves away from design
hyp.key: FI-420 ↓; TCV-401 more open; TI-403 or TI-402 off design
hyp.fals: FI-420 up; TCV-401, TI-402, TI-403, FI-405 at design

hyp.cause: PT-420 reads low: the drum is really at a higher pressure
hyp.ifthen: If the true pressure were higher, less would flash (FI-420 ↓) and the independent PSHH-426 / field PG-420 would read higher than PIC-420
hyp.fals: PG-420 and PSHH-426 agree with PIC-420; FI-420 up

hyp.cause: AI-410 analyser drifting high: the product is really on spec
hyp.ifthen: If only the analyser drifted, the flows and TI-410 would not move and the laboratory bottoms result would be below AI-410
hyp.key: Lab bottoms < AI-410; FI-420, FI-410, TI-410 steady
hyp.fals: Lab agrees with AI-410; FI-420 and TI-410 moved with it

hyp.cause: Feed rate higher than FT-400 shows
hyp.ifthen: If more feed came in, both products would rise: FI-420 ↑ and FI-410 ↑, and FCV-400 would sit more open for the same reading
hyp.key: FI-410 ↑ with FI-420 ↑; FCV-400 off design
hyp.fals: FI-410 falls; FCV-400 at its design opening

hyp.cause: Fuel-gas header or receiver change drawing more vapour
hyp.ifthen: If the header pressure fell, PIC-420 would hold the drum by closing PCV-420; the drum T, P and composition would not change, so AI-410 would not rise
hyp.key: PCV-420 closing; downstream reports a header change; AI-410 steady
hyp.fals: AI-410 and TI-410 move; downstream reports nothing on their side but the tank switch

hyp.cause: A set point or valve was changed on the unit
hyp.ifthen: If someone moved TIC-401, PIC-420 or a bypass, the event log or the field would show it
hyp.key: OPER lines in the event log; a bypass open in the field
hyp.fals: No operator action in the log; all hand valves at their normal position
